answer: Stolen observatory logs were cashing unpaid night slots from a city desk. A watch pays after the observer seats a 1.8-kg onyx baffle on pier 6 of the published dome, tilts an 11-cm first-surface mirror to 37 degrees, and files a 24-second comet trail through an 85 mm lens, locking 19 POA for 6 epochs. Four desks rebuild the centroid track in 0.7 s and must match a 0.3-arcsecond drift plus a 2-pixel FWHM. One key may seat 1 baffle per epoch, so 33 aliases lock 627 POA. A reused baffle serial, or two tracks sharing 21 of 24 timestamps, burns 11 POA and bars that key for 5 epochs.
